title: Skip Crowded Lijiang — Shaxi's Last Tea Caravan Left in 1949 | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone packs into Lijiang. Skip it — a hundred kilometres south sits Shaxi, the Tea-Horse Road town the tour buses forgot.

Shaxi is probably the most intact caravan town left on the ancient Tea-Horse Road — the roughly 1,000-year-old route where caravans swapped Yunnan tea for Tibetan horses. It sits between Dali and Lijiang, about 100 km (3 hours by bus) south of Lijiang. The last caravans passed through in 1949, and the town more or less stopped in time; its old market square was once listed among the world's 100 most endangered sites and later restored.

🧭 Expert Tip: come on a Friday — the Sideng market square still trades, with Bai and Yi villagers bringing produce, supplies and even horses, just as it did on the old caravan route.
